clue.text: Undramatic explanation of depression

parts.note: a depression is a low, an area of low pressure on a weather chart
a key explains the symbols on a map or chart

explanation.surface: Someone describes a quiet, matter-of-fact account of what it's like to feel depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' puts the explanation after what it explains; 'depression' looks emotional but is the weather sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something restrained and subdued, lacking fuss or theatre, is described with this hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Appear to be in charge and make an inspection

parts.note: to appear is to look, as in 'you look tired'
to be over people is to be in charge of them

explanation.surface: A boss turns up to seem in control and carry out an inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal-verb synonym: to examine something quickly is to cast an eye across it, the same as inspecting it.

clue.text: They remove the dead in battles

indicators.note: the dead are placed in the word for battles, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: battles are wars
the dead are gone, departed

explanation.surface: A grim battlefield picture of those who carry away the fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The dead' looks like the object of 'remove', but it is the inner piece; the definition is just 'They remove', i.e. carters who move goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: drivers of horse-drawn carts carry loads away, so they are people who remove things.

clue.text: Having a choice makes them cross

definitions.text: Having a choice makes them cross

parts.words: Having a choice makes them cross
parts.note: voters with a choice of candidates mark a cross on the ballot paper, not angry people

explanation.surface: People given options become irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' seems to mean angry, but it is the X marked on a ballot paper by those choosing a candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: voters given a choice of candidates mark an X on the ballot, so they 'make a cross'.

clue.text: Penalised by being pushed around in the wrong way

indicators.note: pushed goes around the turned word, enclosing it
the wrong way means the little word is turned back to front

explanation.surface: Someone is punished by being shoved about in an improper manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like the anagram signal of 'pushed around', but it is a container: NI, from 'the wrong way', sits within the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone given a penalty for wrongdoing has been disciplined or chastised.

clue.text: A French diet mixed together

parts.note: the French for 'a' is un

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of diet are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A French dietary regime blended up into one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' gives ITED from DIET.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: things joined as one are combined, allied or acting together.

clue.text: Fools do, and it is silly

indicators.note: a silly arrangement scrambles the letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Fools carry on, and the whole thing is daft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges DO IT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: foolish, stupid people are dolts or simpletons.

clue.text: It secures a superior item for ladies

definitions.text: It secures a superior item for ladies

parts.words: It secures a superior item for ladies
parts.note: a long pin holds a woman's hat, the item worn on top, to her hair

explanation.surface: An object fastens some upmarket accessory sold to women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' seems to mean high-quality, but here it means worn on top: the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a long pin fixes a lady's headwear in place, and headwear is the item worn uppermost.

clue.text: Patched up and blooming

definitions.meaning: mended with stitches, as a hole in a sock

explanation.surface: Something repaired and flourishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: repaired by needlework, as socks are; and a mild expletive, as is the British 'blooming'.

clue.text: Rise and go out for drunken binges

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Instructions to get up and head out for a night of heavy drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges RISE and GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: wild parties of drinking and excess are debauched revels or binges.

clue.text: Left with the threat of evil

definitions.meaning: on the left-hand side, the original Latin sense, still used in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone is abandoned with something evil looming.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the Latin word for left-handed, kept in heraldry; and its modern sense of menacing or ominous.

clue.text: Elaborate point to hold forth about

indicators.note: the speechifying word goes about, around, the compass point

parts.note: to hold forth is to orate, speak pompously
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a long speech around some point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elaborate' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective meaning highly decorated.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something intricately decorated and detailed is fancy, ornamented, elaborate.

clue.text: Sit a certain way for the ideal journey?

parts.note: the ideal is the best
a ride is a journey on horseback or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: How to sit to have the perfect trip?
explanation.definitionFit: Description: to sit with one leg on each side, as astride a horse, is a particular way of sitting.

clue.text: Line of defence resulting from counsel's anger

parts.note: counsel are barristers, collectively the bar
rage is anger

explanation.surface: A legal team's fury sets up a defensive line.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar is the legal profession of barristers, who act as counsel in British courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a barrier, such as a dam or an artillery screen, forms an obstructing line of defence.

clue.text: Mother comes back in a frenzy

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: Mum returns home in a wild state.
explanation.walkthrough: A dam is the mother of a horse or other animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone wildly agitated or crazed is frantic, frenzied.

clue.text: Fears loss of an opener to slips

indicators.note: losing the opener means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: terrors are great fears

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: worries about losing an opening batsman to catches in the slips.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opener starts the batting and the slips are fielders behind the batsman; here they are just the first letter and mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: small mistakes or blunders are slips.

clue.text: Don't go without a pen

indicators.note: without means the piece after it is taken away

parts.note: 'don't go' is a plea to stay

explanation.surface: A plea not to leave without a writing implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a biro, but it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an enclosure for pigs is a pen.

clue.text: No alternative

parts.note: the alternative to the reply 'no' is its opposite reply, not 'there is no choice'

explanation.walkthrough: 'No alternative' seems to mean there is no choice, but it is the alternative to the word 'no'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: the other possible answer to a yes-or-no question, the affirmative reply.

clue.text: Track official whose report is eagerly awaited

definitions.text: Track official whose report is eagerly awaited

parts.words: Track official whose report is eagerly awaited
parts.note: the race official fires a pistol, and runners wait for its bang, the report

explanation.surface: An athletics official whose written account everyone is waiting for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' seems a written account, but it is the bang of the pistol that begins a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: the official who begins a race fires a gun, and the runners wait tensely for that shot.

clue.text: Changed class in a rush

indicators.note: the class word is put in the plant word, inside it

parts.note: a rush is a reed, a waterside plant
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A school group altered in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rush' looks like haste, but it is the plant. A form is a British school class.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who has mended their ways has been changed, improved.

clue.text: The first man with a market for water

parts.note: Adam is the first man in Genesis
a sale is a market for goods

explanation.surface: The first man sets up a market to sell water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adam's ale' is a jocular old phrase for plain water, the only drink Adam had.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a humorous name for plain drinking water, the only drink the first man had.

clue.text: Did it make Eve provide some pork?

definitions.text: Did it make Eve provide some pork?

parts.words: Did it make Eve provide some pork?
parts.note: Eve was made from Adam's rib, one he could spare; the same name is a pork cut

explanation.surface: An odd question about whether Eve was turned into a pork supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Eve is formed from one of Adam's ribs, presumably one he could do without.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a cut of pork from the ribs, punning on the extra rib Eve was fashioned from.

clue.text: First start, then finish in ridicule

parts.note: to send off is to start, launch
up means finished, as in 'time is up'

explanation.surface: A sequence of instructions: begin, then end, all in mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a parody or satirical imitation mocks its subject, a form of ridicule.

clue.text: Played truant from desk, perhaps, about four

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the numeral
perhaps means the letters of desk might be ordered another way

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A pupil skipped school from their desk for about four lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the word to SKED, which goes about the numeral. To skive is British slang for dodging work or school.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang synonym: to dodge school or work is to bunk off, play truant.

clue.text: Odd assortment of Biblical characters

parts.note: Biblical, read with characters, gives Job, the patient sufferer of the Old Testament
characters, read with Biblical, gives Lot, Abraham's nephew in Genesis

explanation.surface: A miscellaneous gathering of people from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Biblical characters' covers two Old Testament men, Job and Lot, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Auction-room term: a mixed bundle of items sold together at one price is a miscellaneous assortment.

clue.text: No help as a disinfectant? It could be

indicators.note: 'it could be' says the letters could become another word

explanation.surface: A question whether a disinfectant is useless, with the reply that it could be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It could be' rearranges NO HELP.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: carbolic acid, an early antiseptic, is a disinfectant.

clue.text: An attempt to get past

parts.note: an is the article a
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone makes a try at slipping by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'past' looks like 'get past', going by, but it means previously, in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that happened in the past happened some time before now.

clue.text: Midland footballers out on bail?

indicators.note: out says the letters of the words are put out of order

explanation.surface: Players from a Midlands club released from custody on bail?
explanation.walkthrough: West Bromwich Albion is a football club in the English Midlands. 'out' rearranges ON and BAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the club name of West Bromwich, a Midlands football team, often used for the team itself.

clue.text: Evidence that the deal is not perfect

definitions.text: Evidence that the deal is not perfect

parts.words: Evidence that the deal is not perfect
parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber, and a flaw in such a plank shows it is imperfect

explanation.surface: Proof that a business agreement has flaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' seems a business agreement, but it is softwood timber; a hole left where a branch grew is a flaw in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a hole in timber where a knot has fallen out is a flaw in the wood.

clue.text: Architectural highlight

parts.note: a window jutting from a sloping roof lets light in at the top of a house

explanation.walkthrough: 'highlight' seems to mean a standout feature, but it is a light, a window, set high in the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a window projecting vertically from a sloping roof is a light set high up in a building.

clue.text: Farewell to an Inca ruin in foreign port

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

indicators.note: to ruin is to wreck, so the letters of Inca are wrecked into another order

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to Inca ruins on a trip to an overseas harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruin' rearranges INCA to NCIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Spanish city on the Mediterranean coast with a major seaport.

clue.text: Diminish value of child-bearing

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
an air is one's bearing or manner

explanation.surface: Having a baby lowers the worth of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'child-bearing' looks like one word, but splits into child and bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to damage or weaken something is to lessen its worth or quality.

clue.text: One may lose a whole day going over it

definitions.text: One may lose a whole day going over it

parts.words: One may lose a whole day going over it
parts.note: crossing the Pacific meridian where the calendar changes, a traveller skips a day

explanation.surface: Someone wastes an entire day studying something closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over it' seems to mean reviewing, but it is crossing the line in the Pacific where the calendar date changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: the international boundary at 180 degrees longitude where travellers gain or skip a calendar day.

clue.text: It tells how to break bread with a number inside

indicators.note: the number goes inside the broken-up letters
to break bread means its letters are broken apart and reassembled

parts.note: V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Instructions on breaking bread with a figure in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' turns BREAD into ADERB, and 'inside' puts V within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar description: a word such as 'quickly' modifies a verb, telling how something is done.
